What to do with Doodly

Doodly simulates a hand drawing elements on screen. Pick a background that makes the line art easy to see, keep type large enough for a phone and give each reveal room. A scene explaining a three-step process benefits from a consistent hand style and drawing direction. Preview each scene with the narration before adding decoration.

Building a 60-second product demo

Write three short scenes. Introduce the problem in one frame, draw the solution in the second, and show what the viewer can do next in the third. Time the recording before setting animation duration. A short scene with a single large illustration can carry more information than a crowded canvas with six labels. When a step needs detail, use an extra scene and leave time for the viewer to absorb it.

A practical example

A tutor creates a 45-second lesson on fractions using a circle, three shaded segments and a final worked question. She cuts an extra scene when she finds students can follow the idea from the first drawing alone.

What to review before you finish

The hand reveal controls when information becomes readable. If the voice starts explaining a diagram before the diagram appears, adjust the drawing speed or the narration. Avoid tiny labels at the edges of the canvas. Watch the final output at the size and crop your audience will see.

Preview and export
